standard.title: Use media technologies responsibly
standard.description: explore ways of using media technologies responsibly to capture and organise images, sounds, text and/or interactive elements
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have used digital devices for play and idea exploration. They can capture images or sounds informally. They have not yet explicitly considered responsible use, or deliberately combined visual and audio elements to communicate.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways of using media technologies responsibly to capture and organise images, sounds, text and/or interactive elements.

nodes.label: Responsible use of media technologies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify at least one principle of responsible media technology use and apply it when capturing media elements.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one responsible use principle (e.g. asking permission before taking photos of people) and apply it during a media capture activity.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss and apply responsible use principles when capturing images, sounds and text — including permission to use images of people, care with cultural material, and safe online sharing; connect responsible use to real situations (school excursion photos, class news bulletin).
wider: Develop a class set of rules for using and creating images, sounds and text in media arts works — consulting relevant people (teachers, cultural knowledge holders) and online safety resources, and presenting the rules to the class
Explore what permission means in different contexts (individual permission vs permission for cultural material belonging to a group) through specific case examples
nodes.hinge_reason: Responsible use principles are a prerequisite for all public sharing of student work — if not established here, subsequent presenting and sharing activities lack the ethical grounding that ACARA requires.

response_modes.reason: Use structured scenarios to build reasoning about responsible use — 'Is it OK to take this photo? What do we need to do first?' This develops transferable principles rather than rules memorised for a single context.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one responsible use principle for media technology
Student applies that principle when capturing or sharing media in class activities

nodes.label: Capturing and organising media elements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can capture and organise images, sounds and/or text using a digital device — making deliberate choices about what to capture and how to combine elements.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a digital device to capture at least two types of media elements (e.g. still image and voice-over, or moving image and caption) and organise them to communicate an idea.
nodes.typical_width: Capture, organise and combine images, sound and text across multiple tasks; experiment with how different combinations change meaning; review and select media elements based on communicative purpose; apply Viewpoints questions during capture and review.
wider: Explore how sound communicates ideas by creating sound effects using found objects and integrating them with a picture book or image sequence — experimenting with what changes when different sounds are combined with the same images

Experiment with combining text, symbols and images to communicate emotions or ideas — for example, creating headlines with digital images and comparing how different text changes the meaning of the image

response_modes.reason: Build students' repertoire of capture and combination skills across media types (image, sound, text, moving image) — a broader repertoire means more choices available in later production work.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of media element types (still image, moving image, voice, sound effects, text, symbols) is genuinely rich at Y1-2 — students who explore across types develop much stronger production intuition than those who only use one.
success_criteria: Student captures at least two types of media elements using a digital device
Student organises the elements to communicate an identifiable idea, and can describe one choice they made during organisation

nodes.label: Experimenting to change meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with how changes to media elements (different text, different sound, different framing) change what a work communicates.
nodes.minimum_width: Change at least one element in a media work (e.g. add different text headings to the same image, or move closer/further from a subject) and describe how the change affects meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Systematically experiment with changes to images, sound and text to discover how each change affects meaning; use Viewpoints questions to guide experimentation ('What happens if I take a photo up close?', 'How can I change the meaning of this image by adding different text?'); document discoveries.
wider: Investigate how moving closer to or further from a subject changes the meaning of the captured image — applying Viewpoints questions systematically across a series of distance experiments and comparing results
Explore how adding a voice-over to existing video changes what it communicates — recording multiple different voice-overs for the same footage and comparing the audience experience of each

response_modes.reason: Experimentation to change meaning integrates capture skills with media language understanding — students connect the 'how to do it' (capture) with the 'why it works' (language) by observing the effect of their own changes.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one deliberate change to a media element (text, sound, or framing)
Student can describe how the change affects what the work communicates
